title: HaloQuest hosted embeddings + rerank orientation
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints focused on search relevance for HaloQuest's product catalog. Discussed index options, rerank model mix-in, latency-vs-cost tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and proposed pilot plan with benchmarks and a short POC using their subset of catalog data.
topics: Security: KMS, SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, with Ravi our solutions engineer. Good to meet you all.
[00:08] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): Hi Maya, hi Ravi. Thanks for doing this, our search relevance is kinda the top priority this quarter.
[00:15] Maya Chen (AE): Awesome—today we'll walk through the hosted embeddings and reranker flow, show the console, and outline a low-effort pilot you can run. We'll keep it practical.
[00:24] Ravi Patel (SE): Quick agenda: one, how we generate and serve embeddings; two, retrieval + rerank architecture; three, latency and cost levers (batching, quantization); four, security/compliance stuff; five, next steps.
[00:38] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): Sounds good. For context, we have ~30M SKUs and a product feed that updates hourly. We use an in-house store with a vectordb (FAISS right now) and a microservice stack. Our P95 query latency target is under 200ms from ingress to result, but we've been seeing 400–800ms with our current reranker.
[00:55] Ravi Patel (SE): Got it. A couple clarifying Qs: is your current reranker an on-device smaller model or are you routing to a hosted LLM? And what's your current embeddings dim and vector index config?
[01:06] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): We're using a 768-d embedding from the open-source encoder and FAISS flat index, CPU-only. Reranker is a transformer in a separate service, tuned but hungry on latency.
[01:18] Maya Chen (AE): Helpful. With Redwood hosted inference you can do two patterns: single-call where you call a generation model for ranking, or the more common retrieval + embeddings + lightweight neural rerank step. For most e-commerce customers we recommend the two-step: dense retrieval with embeddings then a specialized reranker on a smaller ranker model to preserve latency cost balance.
[01:36] Anita Roy (HaloQuest/Infosec): From a security standpoint we need SOC2, SSO through our IdP, KMS for keys, and audit logs surfaced to Splunk. Can you cover those?
[01:47] Ravi Patel (SE): Absolutely. Redwood Hosted supports SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS/HSM options). We also emit request-level audit logs that can be routed to your SIEM; we'll show the console audit view.
[01:59] Samir Alami (HaloQuest/CTO): Also interested in data residency — some of our merchants require EU-only storage for PII.
[02:07] Maya Chen (AE): We can pin datasets and model routing by region. For the hosted offering we have EU regions; for strict residency we'd discuss Dedicated or Private later. But for the pilot we can demonstrate EU routing.
[02:19] Ravi Patel (SE): Jumping into the demo—I'll share my screen. Here is the Redwood Console: model catalog, embeddings endpoints, rerank endpoint.
[02:28] [screen share noise]
[02:33] Ravi Patel (SE): Embeddings API is straightforward: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, batch encoding supported up to X items per batch. You can configure dimension and quantized variants. For large catalogs we suggest offline batch encode and store vectors in your DB; then use our vectors-compare endpoint or bring your own FAISS / Milvus.
[02:49] Priya Singh (HaloQuest/Product): When you say "quantized variants"—does that change the embedding quality much? We need relevance preserved for synonyms and typo handling.
[02:57] Ravi Patel (SE): Good Q. Int8 or 4-bit quantization reduces memory and can slightly change distances; in practice for rerank pipelines we often keep full float embeddings for candidate retrieval and apply quantized vectors for cheap similarity lookups in a cache tier. We can A/B compare quality on your prompts during the pilot.
[03:14] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): What about refreshes? Catalog updates hourly — reindexing 30M SKUs each hour is heavy.
[03:20] Maya Chen (AE): Our Optimize toolkit recommends incremental reencode strategies: chunk updates, upsert only changed SKUs, and use prefix caching to reduce QPS for unchanged items. You can schedule background batching jobs and use delta indexes.
[03:31] Ravi Patel (SE): Also, for rerank we support hybrid retrieval (embedding + lexical) so you can fall back on BM25 for cold starts, that often reduces the rerank candidate set and protects latency.
[03:44] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): Could you show a typical request/response for a rerank call? We want to see payload sizes and latency numbers.
[03:50] Ravi Patel (SE): Sure. Here's an example: POST /v1/rerank with original query + top-K candidate passages (id, text, embedding). The rerank model scores and returns ordered ids with scores and optional explanation tokens. Latency for a 10-candidate rerank on our standard rank-small model is ~60ms p95 in hosted for US-west region; if you use a larger cross-attention model it goes up to 180–250ms.
[04:14] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): 60ms p95 sounds good, but end-to-end is what matters. If retrieval is 70ms and network 20ms, adding rerank 60ms hits 150ms which is acceptable. But our current stack right now doesn't batch well and we have spikes.
[04:26] Ravi Patel (SE): You can tune batching and concurrency at the client side. Redwood's SDK supports continuous batching on the runtime, which can merge similar incoming requests to improve throughput while honoring latency SLOs. We can set a max batch latency, or min batch size, whichever you prefer.
[04:40] Priya Singh (HaloQuest): Can the SDK plug into our Java microservices easily?
[04:44] Maya Chen (AE): Yes — we have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a lightweight HTTP guide for Java. The Java guide includes examples for async batching and streaming responses.
[04:53] Anita Roy (HaloQuest/Infosec): On the compliance side: do you keep raw queries and responses? What's the retention and how do we control purge?
[05:00] Ravi Patel (SE): You can configure retention per-tenant—default is 90 days for hosted; enterprise customers can set custom retention windows. For PII-sensitive flows we recommend tokenization before sending, or a Private deployment. We also support an option to disable retention entirely for a given API key.
[05:14] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): Good to know. We'd want an option to redact user-provided PII before hitting the API.
[05:19] Rav i Patel (SE): Yep, we have pre-request hooks and a content filter pipeline you can enable in the console.
[05:26] Samir Alami (HaloQuest/CTO): Back to economics — what's typical per-query cost for the two-step flow?
[05:33] Maya Chen (AE): It depends on model choices and candidate counts. Rough ballpark: embeddings encode (amortized offline) cost is low; retrieval is dominated by your index infra cost; hosted rerank cost for a rank-small model might be $0.0006–$0.002 per call depending on tokenized input size and tokenization. For a 10-candidate rerank across a product description of 100 tokens each, estimate around $0.0012 per query. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet.
[05:57] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): Could we run an experiment with a cheap quantized ranker to validate signals before moving to full model?
[06:03] Ravi Patel (SE): Absolutely—that's the Optimize play: run split tests across quantized vs float rerank models and measure NDCG on your labeled holdout. We'll show the eval harness integration.
[06:13] [10 minutes of screen demo showing console, sample dashboard, audit logs — paraphrased]
[16:20] Ravi Patel (SE): Here's the Console's per-route dashboard. You can see tokens, latency P50/P95/P99, cost by model, and trace links to a request. Notice the fallback policy we configured for high latency windows: it automatically switches to a cheaper ranker or reduces top-K.
[16:39] Priya Singh (HaloQuest): That automatic fallback could be huge for peak shopping hours.
[16:44] Maya Chen (AE): Yep—you can set thresholds and fallback models per route.
[16:49] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): For the pilot, we'd like to use our 500k most active SKUs and run a weekday A/B split — can Redwood handle the ingestion and benchmarking?
[16:57] Ravi Patel (SE): Yes. Typical pilot: ingest subset, run encode job, point your retrieval to either hosted compare endpoint or your existing FAISS index, run live A/B, measure CTR/NDCG and latency. We provide a benchmark spreadsheet template.
[17:12] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): What's the setup time? Our engineers are tight on cycles.
[17:17] Maya Chen (AE): For a lightweight pilot we estimate 2–3 weeks to get meaningful metrics: week one ingestion & encode, week two live A/B and tuning, week three analyze and recommend production rollout. If you want Redwood to do more of the heavy lifting we can assign an onboarding SE.
[17:32] Samir Alami (HaloQuest/CTO): Will dedicated capacity be necessary for us at scale?
[17:37] Ravi Patel (SE): Depends on throughput and SLA needs. Hosted often suffices for initial production tiers; for predictable high-throughput with tighter latency SLOs, a Dedicated pool gives reserved GPUs and network locality. We can model your QPS and recommend.
[17:51] Priya Singh (HaloQuest/Product): Any gotchas with our FAISS setup?
[17:55] Ravi Patel (SE): A few: flat indexes are fast for recall but memory heavy; IVF+PQ reduces memory but affects recall unless you tune nprobe. Also make sure chunking strategy for long product docs is aligned with rerank input expected size. We can provide recommended chunk sizes per model.
[18:09] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): We're worried about billing surprises past the pilot. Does Redwood provide cost alerts?
[18:15] Maya Chen (AE): Yes — Console supports quota enforcement, per-key hard limits, and anomaly alerts on spend. We can also set daily budget caps.
[18:25] Anita Roy (HaloQuest/Infosec): Can you show how audit logs appear? We need to map fields to our SIEM events.
[18:31] Ravi Patel (SE): On the audit view here, each request has time, API key, route, model, token usage, and a hashed user id; you can add correlation ids. We can demo a sample Splunk ingestion via S3 or direct syslog.
[18:46] [minor crosstalk, connection blip at 18:53–19:05]
[19:06] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): OK can we talk success metrics — what should we measure in the pilot?
[19:11] Maya Chen (AE): Suggested: NDCG uplift on labeled queries, CTR change on search results, and tail latency (P95). Set thresholds like +5–7% NDCG or 10% CTR lift as success criteria.
[19:26] Priya Singh (HaloQuest/Product): We have a small labeled dataset of 2k queries; is that enough for a pilot?
[19:31] Ravi Patel (SE): It's enough to get a signal. For robust statistical confidence we'd prefer 5–10k but 2k can reveal directional improvement. We'll integrate with your eval harness.
[19:42] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): Any immediate integration steps we should prep?
[19:46] Maya Chen (AE): Prepare a sample of 500k SKU JSONL, mapping doc_id, title, description, and metadata fields. Also share a small labeled query set, and create an API key for the pilot environment (we can provision).
[19:58] Samir Alami (HaloQuest/CTO): From procurement — what's the pilot cost? Do you discount pilots?
[20:04] Maya Chen (AE): We usually offer a pilot credit and flexible short-term pricing to start. We'll include numbers in the follow-up.
[20:12] Anita Roy (HaloQuest/Infosec): One more security question — what about data in flight? TLS and mutual TLS?
[20:18] Ravi Patel (SE): We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and mTLS for Dedicated/private. Hosted supports standard TLS with client cert options if needed.
[20:28] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): Great. Let's talk timeline — we want to kick off in early May if possible.
[20:33] Maya Chen (AE): That aligns well. We'll propose a kickoff doc.
[20:37] [demo wrap-up and Qs for 5 more minutes — paraphrased]
[26:00] Maya Chen (AE): Quick recap: run a 3-week pilot on 500k SKUs, use hosted embeddings + small reranker, measure NDCG/CTR and P95 latency, compare quantized vs float model. Redwood provides console, audit logs, and an onboarding SE option.
[26:20] Diego Martinez (HaloQuest): Sounds good. Two quick technical follow-ups: 1) we need example code for incremental upserts to FAISS and 2) sample pipeline for offline embedding encode.
[26:32] Ravi Patel (SE): I'll put both in a shared repo — incremental upsert script, and an async encoder job example.
[26:40] Maya Chen (AE): Ok, any other questions?
[26:44] Priya Singh (HaloQuest/Product): None right now.
[26:46] Anita Roy (HaloQuest/Infosec): Not from security.
[26:48] Samir Alami (HaloQuest/CTO): No, thanks.
[26:50] Maya Chen (AE): Great. We'll follow up with the pilot doc, pricing, security packet, and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[26:58] Laura Kim (HaloQuest): Thanks team, excited to try this.
[27:02] Maya Chen (AE): Thanks everyone — we'll send assets within 48 hours.
[27:07] [call ends]

Notes: transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors and occasional mis-attributed speech as is typical for meeting exports. There was a 12s connection blip around 18:53 which removed a short section of audio.
